A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original EEG and MEG retrieval experiments, cross-subject evaluations, retrieval examples, and temporal, spectral, and spatial gradient analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds NSD fMRI retrieval experiments and Harmonization gradient analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed framework retains frozen human-aligned image encoders, trainable brain encoders, symmetric InfoNCE training, and cosine-similarity retrieval. Appendix E applies this framework to fMRI using a cited residual MLP, without revising the proposed alignment or retrieval procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on NSD fMRI responses to MS-COCO natural scenes from four participants. This substantially expands coverage beyond the retained THINGS-based EEG and MEG experiments through both a new measurement modality and a different stimulus corpus.

E2.justification: Harmonization newly participates in the temporal and spectral Grad-CAM comparisons in Appendix G, which previously covered Dreamsim and gLocal. Retrieval comparator membership remains unchanged; the added fMRI experiment reuses the six aligned/base image-encoder pairs.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a separate fMRI protocol: individual residual-MLP encoders, 24,980 unaveraged training samples, test-response averaging to 982 unique samples, and retrieval reported as 1000-way. It specifies 50 epochs, learning rate 0.0001, and batch size 128. Existing EEG/MEG settings are retained; new Section 4.4 explains their existing retrieval metrics.

E4.justification: v2 extends the existing temporal and spectral Grad-CAM analyses to Harmonization with ConvNeXT, LEViT, ResNet-50, and VGG16, examining gradient patterns where alignment helps or hurts retrieval. These additions appear in Figures 12–13 and 18–19. Earlier Dreamsim/gLocal analyses and retrieval case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe five seeds, uncertainty reporting, paired retrieval-performance t-tests, and unpaired spectral tests. The added tables and plots follow existing reporting practices; no increased run count or new statistical estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial fMRI results in Tables 8–9; for example, Table 8 reports SynCLR mean top-1 accuracy of 58.2 ± 4.6 for aligned embeddings versus 48.2 ± 4.3 for base embeddings. It also adds Harmonization gradient findings and corrects Table 2's S1 aligned OpenCLIP value from 1.5 ± 0.55 to 11.5 ± 0.55. Other matched EEG/MEG retrieval values are retained.

T1.justification: The embedding formulation, InfoNCE objective, periodogram definition, and Fourier-transform equation are unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical proofs, and the added retrieval-metric explanation does not change a mathematical definition or formal property.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims that human alignment improves visual decoding across encoders and modalities, with reported improvements up to 21% and a proposed early-perception explanation. The new experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 connects Harmonization's temporal and spectral gradient patterns to architectures where alignment improves or degrades retrieval. It also explains choosing retrieval to isolate alignment effects and adds substantive applicability limits: controlled laboratory use and lack of validation on patient data.

D1.justification: v2 provides an explicit project-code URL, documents the fMRI encoder and training settings, and identifies the previously unnamed Figure 4 example as participant S4 with SynCLR. Existing EEG/MEG preprocessing, model-source listings, and training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lin et al. on MS-COCO and Takagi and Nishimoto on fMRI reconstruction to support the new experiment. Research positioning otherwise remains stable. The Muttenthaler citation-year changes concern the same previously cited works.

P1.justification: v2 adds an evaluation subsection, an Impact Statement, and an fMRI appendix, alongside localized grammatical and terminology edits. The existing argument and section sequence are largely retained, with later appendices renumbered to accommodate the addition.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual material through two fMRI tables and four multi-panel Harmonization figures. It also redraws the Figure 2 workflow, increases Figure 5's image resolution, and clarifies Figure 4's caption. Earlier appendix galleries and Dreamsim/gLocal plots are retained despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The NSD fMRI experiment provides useful validation beyond THINGS-based EEG/MEG, while the Harmonization diagnostics help assess alignment failures. Clearer evaluation documentation and an explicit code location also improve transparency. These gains are tempered by incomplete integration: Section 6 still presents fMRI as future work, and Appendix E leaves the relationship between 982 unique test samples and its 1000-way retrieval labeling unexplained.
